caption:
Ignore the short fuse you bring home, and your kids will pay for it in silence. 👇

Shoes in the hallway.
The TV too loud.
A simple question at the wrong time.
And you snap. Then you feel terrible the rest of the night.

Here's what's really happening:
All day you held it in. The boss. The pressure. The "I'm fine."
You can't let it out at work, because you can't risk that job.
So the second you walk through the door, it comes out on the people who feel safest.

And you're not the only one holding it in. In Monster's 2026 workplace mental health report, 7 in 10 workers said they feel pressure to appear "okay" at work. All that pressure has to go somewhere.

Why it matters: your kids don't know about your boss. They just learn to tiptoe around you. They get quieter. They stop telling you things.

The fix: say it out loud before it comes out sideways.
Walk in and tell them: "I'm not mad at you. I had a hard day. Give me 10 minutes."
Take the 10 minutes. Then come back as you.

The sun's still shining over that house. Make sure the people inside get the best of you, not what's left.

What sets YOU off after a hard day? Be honest. 👇
